are loaded from a single `.RData` file produced by the preparation notebook. This object (`metrics`) is a long-format data frame with one row per participant, date, wearing position, and metric. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .hidden} #| label: import-metrics load(here("data/prepared_metrics.RData")) ``` ::: ## Visualizing metrics A few shared plotting helpers are defined here: a log-scale break sequence, a named color vector (one color per wearing position), and a number formatter for axis labels. ::: {.cell filename='helpers'} ```{.r .cell-code .hidden} #| label: plot-helpers #| filename: helpers breaks <- c(0, 10^(0:5)) colors <- ggsci::pal_jco()(3) |> set_names(c("glasses", "chest", "wrist")) label <- function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = " ") ``` ::: ## Preparing metric table The raw metrics data frame is restructured for per-metric modelling. Factor levels are set for `position`, `Id`, `site`, and `Date` (missing dates are replaced with a sentinel value so they don't drop). The data are then nested so that each row in `metrics_nested` holds all observations for a single metric. ::: {.cell filename='nest data'} ```{.r .cell-code .hidden} #| label: nest-metrics #| filename: nest data metrics_nested <- metrics |> mutate(Date = replace_na(Date, as_date("2024-09-01")), position = factor(position, levels = c("glasses", "chest", "wrist")), Id = factor(Id), site = factor(site), Date = factor(Date)) |> nest(data = -c(metric)) ``` ::: Metadata for each metric (model engine, response transformation, metric type, etc.) is read from an Excel file. The `engine` column determines which modelling function to use (`lm`, `lmer`, `glmer`, `glmmTMB`), and the corresponding distributional family is constructed here. The metadata is then joined onto the nested data frame so every metric row knows how it should be modelled. ::: {.cell filename='Load metric information'} ```{.r .cell-code .hidden} #| label: load-metric-info #| filename: Load metric information metric_info <- read_xlsx(here("data/metric_types.xlsx")) metric_info <- metric_info |> mutate(family = map(engine, \(x) switch(x, "lm" = gaussian(), "lmer" = gaussian(), "glmer" = poisson(), "glmmTMB" = tweedie(link = "log"))), family = map2(family, note, \(x,y) ifelse(is.na(y), return(x), return(poisson())) ) ) |> select(-note) ``` ::: ::: {.cell filename='Combine metric data and metadata'} ```{.r .cell-code .hidden} #| label: join-metric-metadata #| filename: Combine metric data and metadata metrics_nested <- metrics_nested |> left_join(metric_info, by = join_by(metric == name)) ``` ::: ### Scaling nighttime metrics Metrics that capture timing and might cross midnight need to be rescaled in order to work with linear models. width=1440} ::: ::: ## Prepare modelling The primary hypothesis (H1) is that wearing position affects a metric, potentially differently across measurement sites (i.e., a `site × position` interaction). The right-hand side of the formula is assembled here by appending the pre-specified random-effects structure (stored in the `random` column of `metric_info`) to the fixed-effects template `~ site*position`. A helper then collects all formula column names (H0 and H1 variants) for programmatic iteration. The table below summarises the modelling specification for every metric: the response variable, any pre-transformation applied, the modelling engine, the distributional family, and the full H1 formula. Confirmatory analyses deliberately omit p-value correction, because a *non-significant* position effect is the more scientifically desirable outcome. ::: {.cell filename='Add formulas'} ```{.r .cell-code .hidden} #| label: add-formulas #| filename: Add formulas metrics_nested <- metrics_nested |> mutate(H1 = paste0("~ site*position", random)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell filename='Collect models'} ```{.r .cell-code .hidden} #| label: collect-formula-names #| filename: Collect models Formulas <- names(metrics_nested) |> subset(grepl("H1|H0_", names(metrics_nested))) ``` ::: ::: {#tbl-model-specs .cell} ```{.r .cell-code .hidden} #| label: tbl-model-specs #| echo: false metrics_nested |> select(-data, -random) |> arrange(metric_type, metric_family, metric) |> mutate(family = map(family, 1), rowname = seq_along(1:length(metric))) |> group_by(metric_type) |> gt() |> cols_label_with(fn = \(x) x |> str_to_title() |> str_replace_all("_", " ")) |> sub_missing(missing_text = "") |> sub_values(values = "NULL", replacement = "") |> fmt(c(metric, pre.transformed, response), fns = \(x) x |> str_to_title() |> str_replace_all("_", " ")) |> sub_values(values = "MDER", replacement = "MDER") |> tab_header("Metric model specifications", subtitle = "Hypothesis: wearing position affects metric result within sites") |> tab_footnote("Confirmatory analysis will use no p-value correction, as a non-significant difference result is the more desired result") |> tab_footnote("These are the models used for the analysis per metric.
